findings.title: error-invalid-multivalued-size converted from i18next to Java MessageFormat syntax, breaking display in the account UI
findings.body: This file is consumed by the React account UI, which uses i18next with `{{placeholder}}` interpolation (every other entry in the file uses `{{0}}`, `{{name}}`, etc.). The changed line now reads `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` — i18next will not interpolate `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}`, and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` is Java MessageFormat choice syntax that i18next does not parse. When the server-side multivalued-attribute validation error is displayed in the account UI, users will see the raw template text including the literal choice-format string instead of a formatted message.

findings.title: error-invalid-multivalued-size converted from i18next to Java MessageFormat syntax, breaking display in the admin UI
findings.body: This file backs the React admin UI, which renders server validation error keys via i18next `t(key, params)` using `{{0}}`-style interpolation (the previous value used `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}`). The new value `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` uses Java MessageFormat placeholders and a `{2,choice,...}` clause that i18next cannot evaluate, so the admin console will show the literal unformatted string (including the choice syntax) when the multivalued attribute size validation fails.

findings.title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: In the Lithuanian (lt) translation file, `totpStep1` was changed from a Lithuanian sentence (which contained anchor tags the new verifier rejects) to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` — that is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will now see an Italian sentence in the account console OTP setup instructions. The replacement should be a Lithuanian equivalent of "Install one of the following applications on your mobile:".

findings.title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: In the Lithuanian login messages, `loginTotpStep1` was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. This appears to be a copy-paste error when removing the anchor-containing Lithuanian text to satisfy the new HTML verifier; the login OTP setup page will show Italian text to Lithuanian users.

findings.title: Traditional Chinese text inserted into the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) file
findings.body: `totpStep1` in the zh_CN account messages was changed to `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`, which uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 應用程式, 安裝) — apparently copied from the zh_TW phrasing. The rest of the zh_CN file uses Simplified Chinese (e.g. 应用, 手机), so the account console will show an inconsistent, wrong-variant sentence to mainland-Chinese users. It should read something like `在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：`.

findings.title: Missing or unreadable English counterpart file throws a bare RuntimeException instead of a proper build error
findings.body: `verify()` wraps file reading in a catch that converts IOException into a descriptive MojoExecutionException, but the new `verifySafeHtml()` catches IOException from reading the message file or the computed `_en.properties` counterpart and rethrows it as an unchecked RuntimeException (lines 66-80). If a translation file is processed whose English counterpart does not exist (e.g. a newly added locale, or a file outside the expected directory layout), the Maven build aborts with a raw RuntimeException stack trace rather than a clean verification message or MojoExecutionException, making failures harder to diagnose and bypassing the plugin's documented error handling.

findings.title: Anchor check compares tags positionally and the pattern matches any tag starting with 'a', causing false positives
findings.body: `santizeAnchors` matches the N-th anchor in the translation against the N-th anchor in the English source and requires exact string equality. A legitimate translation that reorders two links (common when target-language word order differs) is rejected with "Didn't find anchor tag" even though it contains exactly the same anchors. Additionally, the pattern `</?a[^>]*>` matches any tag beginning with 'a' (`<abbr>`, `<address>`, `<article>`, ...), so those tags are silently stripped from the compared value when they happen to positionally match an English 'anchor', or produce misleading "Didn't find anchor tag" messages instead of being validated by the HTML policy. Both cases produce false verification failures for valid translations.
